title: Private resident reports with bounded zero-dollar infrastructure

authorization.current_action: Parent reviewed the proposal, integrated retention/replay/restore corrections, and is committing the proposal and linked decisions. This does not approve a provider or authorize provisioning.
authorization.parent_action: T12 is complete as a decision-ready proposal only. T13 remains an explicit owner gate; T14-T18 are not completed by this artifact.

local_contracts.requirement: Concrete provider, storage, abuse, owner access, retention and failure proposal before infrastructure approval or implementation.
Separate mapping errors and shelter requests; private reports; server-owned receipt and moderation state; no contact details or implicit provider approval.
Truthful durable receipts, idempotency, access control, lifecycle, abuse limits and deletion tests.

components: Separate Workers Free moderator application protected by Access Free
recommendation.frontend: Retain the existing Vercel frontend; submit directly to the reporting Worker, without a Vercel function proxy.
recommendation.domain: Use provider-issued workers.dev hostnames; no purchased domain is required for the proposal.
recommendation.reason: A transactional database and private moderator application fit the report lifecycle. Free-plan request and database limits fail rather than authorize metered overages; a low-volume service can therefore remain at zero provider spend with explicitly accepted availability limits.
recommendation.claim_boundary: Feasible design under current documented Free plans, not a deployed service, availability guarantee, contractual perpetual price guarantee or approved infrastructure choice.

costs_and_provider_quotas.engineering_time_estimate: Not estimated by this research; implementation and controlled backend validation remain work in T14-T18.
hard_zero_conditions: Explicitly verify Workers Free, D1 Free and Access Free before provisioning or activation.
Do not use an existing Workers Paid account on the assumption that unused included allowances provide a hard zero-dollar cap.
No paid add-ons, paid plan conversion, automatic upgrade authorization, purchased domain or billed backup service is included.
Keep fail-closed behavior. When free limits are exhausted, accept unavailable reporting rather than paid overages.
Application counters and alerts are operational controls, not a substitute for selecting a non-billed plan.
costs_and_provider_quotas.spend_cap_distinction: A free allowance inside a paid plan is not a hard spend cap. This proposal relies on non-paid plans and documented quota rejection, not on a provider-wide configurable dollar cap. It does not promise uninterrupted service or protection from future plan changes.

limits.exhaustion: Daily request exhaustion returns Cloudflare error 1027. CPU or memory exhaustion can return error 1102. Shared account usage includes both reporting Workers.
Daily read/write exhaustion rejects queries. Storage exhaustion prevents new data and affected schema/index operations until space is reclaimed.
accounting_cautions: Rows read are not the same as query count.
Indexes add written rows and storage.
Maintenance and dashboard queries consume quota too.
Daily enforcement was explicitly announced effective 2026-09-01.

limits.challenges_and_verifications: Unlimited under the published Free plan

public_api.endpoint: POST /v1/reports on the public submission Worker
public_api.cors: Allow only approved frontend origins and required methods/headers. CORS is not authentication or bot protection.
public_api.service_worker: Never cache report requests, responses, secrets or private moderation content.

moderator_api.deployment: Separate Worker serving a private queue and lifecycle API
moderator_api.access_scope: Protect the entire Worker, including production domains and preview URLs; no hostname or preview bypass.
moderator_api.authorization: Deny by default, then allow only the explicitly approved moderator identity.

database.access: D1 bindings only in the two server Workers; no database binding or account token in resident JavaScript.
database.query_policy: Parameterized queries, bounded indexed listing and no generic SQL endpoint.
database.least_privilege_limit: D1 bindings grant broad database capability. Separate code paths are an application security boundary, not per-table or per-resident database roles.

secrets.storage_rule: Owner-approved local secret storage and provider secrets only; never commit secrets or expose them through URLs, evidence or browser logs.

optional_context: six-digit postal code when attached to a selected postal

geometry.coordinate_order: longitude, latitude, explicitly normalized at the UI/API boundary
geometry.validation: Finite numeric coordinates within a reviewed Singapore service boundary, with a point or bounded segment appropriate to the report type.
geometry.unresolved_detail: T14 must pin the exact service-boundary constants and existing geometry helper used for validation; no boundary or route generation is authorized here.

payload.text_handling: Render notes as plain text, never executable HTML. Warn residents not to enter personal information; automatic rejection of contact fields does not guarantee that free text contains no personal information.

current_code_reduction.finding: Do not persist the clipboard payload wholesale. Its existing single correction issue also does not distinguish mapping errors from shelter requests.

acceptance_semantics.shelter_request: Accepted for consideration; does not establish that a shelter exists or promise construction.
acceptance_semantics.mapping_error: Accepted for investigation/correction; evidence and a separately approved versioned release are required before published routes change.

idempotency_and_receipts.request_identity: Random client request ID plus independently generated 256-bit retry secret; only the secret hash is stored server-side.
idempotency_and_receipts.payload_identity: Canonical validated report-content hash, excluding replaceable challenge tokens and transport fields.
idempotency_and_receipts.atomic_write: Unique request identity, report insertion, quota consumption and initial audit event commit together. Avoid separate read-then-insert accounting.
idempotency_and_receipts.same_id_same_payload: Require the matching retry secret and return the original receipt metadata without a second report or quota debit. Authenticate an existing committed request separately from fresh Turnstile verification: an expired or already-used challenge must not prevent receipt recovery. Keep bounded transport/authentication abuse controls on this replay path.
idempotency_and_receipts.same_id_changed_payload: Return 409 after authenticating the retry; never overwrite the first report.
idempotency_and_receipts.receipt: Return 201 only after durable database commit. A receipt contains server identity/time and confirms receipt, not verification or acceptance.
idempotency_and_receipts.ambiguous_timeout: Retain draft and request identity. Retry the same submission to resolve whether the original commit succeeded.
idempotency_and_receipts.secret_handling: No secrets in URLs, shared links, remote logs or public evidence. No report-body lookup using a receipt identifier alone.
idempotency_and_receipts.bounded_retry_requirement: T14 must define a server-enforceable request expiry and retain minimal deduplication tombstones through that validity period. Deletion must not allow an expired request to create a new report. The mechanism and exact lifetime are unresolved; this proposal does not claim unbounded idempotency.

abuse_and_application_caps.quota_atomicity: Global/day, pending and retained limits are checked and updated inside the database transaction that admits a new report.
pre_database_controls: server-side Turnstile verification before admitting a new report, not as a prerequisite to authenticated committed-receipt recovery

turnstile.load_policy: Load a managed widget only when composing a report, not on map browsing.
turnstile.validation_retry: Use Siteverify idempotency_key for retries of a verification request. This is separate from application report idempotency.

abuse_and_application_caps.rate_limiter_limit: Cloudflare's Worker rate limiter is location-local, permissive and eventually consistent. It is not an exact global counter or financial accounting system.
abuse_and_application_caps.ip_limit_limit: Shared networks can inconvenience legitimate residents; distributed traffic can evade per-IP buckets. No promise of complete spam prevention.
abuse_and_application_caps.privacy: Use rotating keyed HMAC buckets and purge from the active store within 48 hours, subject to the documented cleanup/outage limitation. Provider recovery history can retain pre-deletion buckets for up to seven additional days; exclude abuse buckets from independent backups. Do not store raw IPs or user agents in report rows. Cryptographic hashing does not by itself make request metadata anonymous.

capacity_arithmetic.validation_required: Measure actual storage and rows_read/rows_written on synthetic admission, retry, moderation and cleanup operations in T18. Report count is not a proven database quota budget.

failure_behavior.application_limit: 429 with bounded retry advice; no receipt for a rejected new report.
failure_behavior.backend_or_challenge_unavailable: 503 or a truthful unavailable UI; retain the draft and request identity.
failure_behavior.provider_level_failure: Cloudflare may return HTML, a resource-limit error or a network failure before application code runs. The browser must handle non-JSON responses without displaying success.
failure_behavior.authentication_failure: Deny queue access and mutations; retain no private content in an unauthenticated response.
failure_behavior.partial_or_ambiguous_commit: Use the original authenticated idempotency identity on retry, not a fresh report ID.
failure_behavior.quota_attack: Attack traffic can exhaust the shared Free account request or query budget and prevent reporting or moderation until reset. Separate Workers do not create separate account quotas.
no_fallbacks: clipboard success presented as server submission
failure_behavior.map_independence: Reporting failure must not disable existing published walks or map browsing.
failure_behavior.logs: No report notes, full coordinates, tokens, request bodies or contact information in application logs.

privacy_and_retention.report_content_expiry: Earlier of 90 days after receipt or 30 days after resolution.
privacy_and_retention.cleanup: Daily bounded deletion with indexed expiry queries; queries suppress expired report content immediately. Check cleanup health and capacity before admitting new reports.
privacy_and_retention.early_deletion: Moderator can delete accidental personal information promptly. T13 must approve any resident withdrawal mechanism; do not expose report bodies through a deletion capability.
privacy_and_retention.audit_policy: Delete or minimize associated private audit details and secrets under the same approved retention policy. Expiring report text while retaining equivalent text in audit rows is not deletion.
privacy_and_retention.backup_residue: D1 Time Travel can recover pre-deletion data for up to seven days. SQL deletion is not immediate erasure from recovery history.
privacy_and_retention.restore_rule: Reapply deletion/expiry rules before reopening access after restoration. Keep an approved minimal early-deletion ledger independently of the restored snapshot and through every applicable recovery window, with no report text or location. A ledger rolled back with the database cannot prevent resurrection. If the independent ledger is unavailable or inconsistent, do not reopen restored report access.
privacy_and_retention.outage_limit: Provider or quota outages can delay physical deletion. This proposal does not promise an unconditional 90-day physical-erasure deadline; the owner must approve realistic cleanup and incident handling.
privacy_and_retention.provider_processing: Turnstile processes IP address, TLS/browser signals and associated origin. No resident login does not mean anonymous or zero-personal-data processing.
privacy_and_retention.provider_retention_uncertainty: The reviewed Turnstile Privacy Addendum does not specify a numerical retention period for its signals. SHIOK's report-row policy cannot be represented as controlling all provider security metadata.
privacy_and_retention.residency: APAC is a placement hint, not guaranteed Singapore-only storage or processing. D1 documents EU and FedRAMP jurisdictions, not a Singapore jurisdiction. Do not make a Singapore-residency claim.
privacy_and_retention.legal_boundary: This is a technical proposal, not a legal compliance determination. Owner approval of privacy notice, provider terms and applicable obligations remains required.

backups_and_operations.built_in_recovery: D1 Free seven-day Time Travel; same-provider/account recovery is not an independent backup.
backups_and_operations.proposed_independent_backup: Weekly encrypted owner-controlled export, retained no longer than seven days, in a separately approved private destination outside public Git/evidence. Exclude short-lived abuse buckets. Keep the approved early-deletion ledger independently from the snapshot being restored; validate retention and deletion before reopening access.
backups_and_operations.cost_constraint: No paid backup provider is authorized or included. Use an owner-approved existing destination only after its privacy, capacity and retention are accepted.
backups_and_operations.maximum_expected_backup_loss_window: Up to seven days between successful weekly exports; missed exports increase this window. Not a guaranteed recovery objective.
backups_and_operations.moderation_cadence_proposal: Owner reviews the private queue twice weekly, removes accidental personal information promptly and disables intake when unable to keep up.
backups_and_operations.moderation_ui: Filter by type/state/date; inspect location and bundle context; accept/reject/mark duplicate with reason; show revision and decision time. Queue is separate from the resident map.
backups_and_operations.no_contact_consequence: No emailed decision or follow-up interview with residents is available without changing the approved no-contact scope.
incident_actions: preserve private incident evidence only under approved policy
restore only through an approved procedure
revalidate access and deletion rules before reopening

provider_comparison.option: Cloudflare Workers Free + D1 Free + Turnstile Free + Access Free
constraints: provider security metadata is not governed by report-row retention
independent backup and moderator time remain owner responsibilities

provider_comparison.reason: Free projects may pause after a low-activity seven-day period. That creates avoidable owner intervention for a small reporting queue. Paid spend caps do not convert a paid plan into a zero-dollar plan.

Spark is genuinely no-cost, but the conventional Cloud Functions server-side enforcement path requires Blaze and a billing account. A split external backend can avoid that path but adds complexity without improving this recommendation. Do not treat Blaze's included allowances or budget alerts as a hard zero-dollar cap.

provider_comparison.option: Public GitHub issues, clipboard JSON or browser-only storage
provider_comparison.reason: Public issues violate report privacy; clipboard/local state does not supply a durable server receipt. These are not equivalent reporting services.
Still requires a secure submission service, moderator access controls, concurrency-safe identity, retention and abuse handling. It does not remove the important implementation work.

owner_decisions.decision: Approve Cloudflare and verify that the designated Workers, D1 and Access plans are Free, including accepting required Access payment-method onboarding.
Approve minimized payload, provider processing/residency disclosures, report retention, early deletion, backup residue and realistic outage handling.
Approve submission/backlog/storage caps, shared-network trade-offs, challenge UX and temporarily unavailable reporting instead of paid scaling.
Name the moderator, approve authentication and twice-weekly review, and identify the operator who disables intake during absence or incidents.
Approve private encrypted backup destination, keys, seven-day retention, early-deletion handling and accepted recovery loss window.
Create/designate account, enable MFA, retain recovery credentials and provide only scoped credentials through approved secret storage. No secret is requested in chat or committed evidence.

Authorize provisioning, necessary tooling and synthetic backend validation explicitly. Complete T14-T18 and obtain release approval before enabling production submission; a general completion goal does not erase these gates.

required_validation_before_activation: F01/F13: both report types, minimized fields, no resident account/contact/photo requirement.
F02/F03: nonfinite and out-of-bound geometry, oversized streamed body, note and unknown-field rejection, inert markup rendering.
F04/F06: actual durable commit before receipt; timeout after commit and non-JSON provider errors preserve truthful state.
F05: concurrent same-ID submissions, changed payload, wrong retry secret, quota debit once, deletion/tombstone/expiry boundaries.
F07: public listing/body lookup denied, forged/expired/wrong-audience JWT rejected, alternate production/preview host protection, unauthorized moderator, CSRF and XSS.
F08-F10: revision races, reason/audit requirements, duplicate cycles and no published-data mutation.
F11: global cap races, per-IP caveats, challenge expiry/replay/timeout, request/read/write/storage exhaustion, kill switch and actual per-operation quota accounting.
F12: synthetic retention cleanup, early deletion, missed cleanup, backup deletion, restoration without resurrecting expired/private content.
End-to-end: controlled synthetic submission and moderator retrieval against an explicitly approved real backend, without using real resident data.
Local fixtures or green tests alone do not establish a deployed durable reporting service.
findings: A bounded zero-dollar service is feasible under the documented Cloudflare Free plans if temporary unavailability is accepted; free allowances inside paid plans are not equivalent.
Access Free still requires payment details during onboarding, an unavoidable owner action for the recommended authentication choice.
Worker rate limiting is not globally exact; transactional application caps are still needed.
Seven-day database recovery, independent backups and provider security signals make immediate total erasure an unsupported promise.
The existing clipboard report shape includes unnecessary score/path detail and does not yet implement distinct durable report types.
No provider has been approved and T13-T18 remain open; this research does not authorize provisioning or deployment.

Review corrected three proposal ambiguities: 48-hour abuse-bucket retention describes active storage rather than all recovery copies; authenticated committed-receipt recovery must survive challenge expiry; and a deletion ledger must survive independently of the snapshot being restored.
disagreements: None with the approved private, no-resident-account, no-contact, no-photo direction. The proposal rejects interpreting hard zero-dollar spend as guaranteed service availability or zero provider processing of personal data.

Explicit daily Free row-limit enforcement and corresponding error behavior.

Worker-level protection covering associated domains and preview URLs.
Account/MFA setup and payment details required even when selecting Zero Trust Free.

Bindings grant server resource capabilities without embedding account credentials in frontend code.
Parameterized statements and batch transaction rollback.
Server verification, five-minute single-use tokens and validation idempotency_key.
Permissive, per-location, eventually consistent limits are not an accurate accounting system.
Point-in-time recovery and seven-day Free history.
IP, TLS/browser signals, origin and provider processing roles; no numerical signal-retention period found in this addendum.
